scope: Fresh Batch Worker startup with Messaging reliability and runtime-control auto-configurations
rootCause: CpfBrokerReliabilityAutoConfiguration unconditionally creates cpfBrokerConsumerRuntimePolicy while CpfMessagingRuntimeControlAutoConfiguration also creates a conditional fallback. Without explicit auto-configuration ownership order and main-owner backoff, both definitions survive and Worker injection is ambiguous.
actualError: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException: expected single CpfBrokerConsumerRuntimePolicy but found brokerConsumerRuntimePolicy and cpfBrokerConsumerRuntimePolicy
requiredFix: Make Reliability the ordered main policy owner, let both paths honor an application-provided policy, and add a composed auto-configuration context regression asserting one policy and one Worker.
prohibited: Do not mark an arbitrary duplicate @Primary, qualify different policy instances, disable messaging reliability, or hide the failure in smoke configuration.

sourceFix.implementation: Reliability is ordered before runtime-control and both policy definitions back off to an existing application or owner bean.
sourceFix.regression: Composed ApplicationContextRunner supplies the mandatory named broker Provider and verifies one shared policy and one Worker with default and application override cases.
